overview.text: The Petrovskaya icon is named for Saint Peter, Metropolitan of Moscow. Its church history and the seventeenth-century example displayed here are separately identified.

blocks.text: The pictured icon is a later example by Nazary Istomin Savin in the Tretyakov Gallery. Its file title gives 1614 while structured metadata gives 1616; both place this work in the seventeenth century. It is not labelled as Peter’s own medieval panel.

blocks.text: The OCA recounts Peter painting an icon while abbot near Volhynia and giving it to Metropolitan Maximus. After Maximus’s death, the account connects the icon with Gerontius’s attempted journey to Constantinople and Peter’s eventual consecration. A vision of the Mother of God belongs to that ecclesiastical narrative.

blocks.text: The narrative identifies Maximus as metropolitan of Kiev and all Russia and dates his repose to 1306. Its changing episcopal centers explain the subsequent movement through Vladimir and Moscow.

blocks.text: The source follows the icon to Vladimir and then Moscow in 1325, where it is placed in the Dormition Cathedral. It prints August 24 for its commemoration. The historical Savin example illustrates the continuation of a named iconographic tradition rather than documenting an unbroken physical history of the original.
